prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / map art-direction iteration.
Create a revised full-map image for Tequila Kill based on REFERENCE 1. Keep its softly shaded pixel-art western village, large open rooms, large central square, small furniture and exactly FOUR small character silhouettes. Apply the newly approved visual principles: UNMISTAKABLE WALKABLE OPENINGS, SOLID PERMANENT OBSTACLES, and A COHERENT FAMILY OF BREAKABLE PROPS.

REFERENCE 1 is the BASE MAP to revise. Preserve its general building positions, overall 16:10 full-map framing, camera and gentle warm shading.
REFERENCE 2 is ONLY A FUNCTIONAL VISUAL EXAMPLE from Zelda: a wall with damage becomes an actual visible hole. Use that clarity of geometry and change of state. Do NOT copy Zelda colors, HUD, text, room layouts or characters. Do NOT make our permanent building walls destructible.

PRIORITY 1 — ACTUAL VISIBLE HOLES IN WALLS:
The previous drawing still showed opaque door leaves, wall faces, posts or lintels where the player should walk. Fix this in the DRAWING itself.
For every accessible opening described below, REMOVE the whole obstructing wall section, header beam, door leaf, sill and any central post. The wall must visibly END on both sides of a wide gap. Leave low terminated wall ends. Continuous floor tiles or wooden threshold planks should visibly pass through the gap into the outside walk area; nothing upright spans or fills that passage. Use the equivalent of a clear open breach, not a drawn closed doorway. No diagonal opaque wall face hiding the gap. No archway overhead that obscures the ground. Each gap comfortably allows at least two of the depicted characters side by side, with empty approach space both inside and outside.
On the approximately 1600 x 1000 base image, make these very concrete cuts:
A SALOON, left large room: remove its EAST wall across the central facing-the-square section, approximately x=590-655 and y=470-620, to create a very broad clear side entrance. The blue-gray interior floor extends all the way to the empty threshold and becomes sand/wood outside. Also remove its SOUTH wall across approximately x=280-420, y=700-750, creating a second broad exit toward the lower street. No front facade or door panel crosses either gap.
B GENERAL STORE, right large room: remove its WEST wall across approximately x=1030-1100, y=500-635, creating an unmistakable wide entry toward the square. Also remove its SOUTH wall across approximately x=1190-1340, y=700-750 for a second separate clear exit. Do not redraw the current opaque brown leaf or thin corner post in these spaces.
C STORAGE SHED lower-left: remove its SOUTH wall across x=290-405, y=920-952, plus its EAST wall across x=480-525, y=835-915. Both are open walk-through gaps, not closed doors or merely steps on the outside of an intact wall.
D FENCED YARD upper-right: create two obvious empty fence gaps, one in its LEFT edge around x=1180-1210,y=180-265 and one in its LOWER edge around x=1280-1400,y=305-335. The fence ends in posts outside the gaps; NO rails across them.
These coordinates explain areas in the reference, not a required diagram. Do not draw coordinates, colored bands, arrows, rings or overlay.
Closed residential houses remain closed background dwellings with their existing roofs and doors. The open breach rule applies only to accessible gameplay buildings and the yard. Keep the existing main street and both outside routes continuous. Remove any isolated railing that accidentally seals a loop or forces a one-person choke. Do not block a clear opening with pots, crates, chairs, characters or decorative trim.

PRIORITY 2 — FUNCTIONAL CONTRAST:
Calm light golden sand, very subtle blue-gray tile grout, restrained timber/roof texture, soft warm gradients inside crisp stepped pixel-art silhouettes. Permanent collision masses have a clean continuous medium-dark brown outline, slightly clearer than in reference 1 so players can read where a wall ENDS. No uniform black outline on every decorative detail. No blurry edges, overall haze or grey wash.
Keep the bright sunny western palette; do not turn the scene into a dark blue TowerFall cave. Quiet background details, clear room/street geometry, small saturated character accents. Retain generous empty combat floor, no new big landmarks or added buildings.

PRIORITY 3 — READABLE BREAKABLE PROPS, FOLLOW THE ACTUAL CATEGORIES:
BREAKABLE: wooden CRATES, light wooden CHAIRS, terracotta POTS.
PERMANENT: building WALLS, heavy COUNTERS, SHELVES, TABLES, COUCH, BARRELS and CART.
Do not communicate that barrels, large tables or walls are breakable. Give heavy permanent furniture sturdy dark framing and intact continuous silhouettes.
Give ALL breakable crates/chairs/pots a shared subtle but clear material language: more luminous warm ochre/clay body, a crisp pale warm edge highlight and visibly light/thin construction. Crates have a few clearly separated loose boards, small corner chips, a dark simple notch in the top plank, NO heavy iron corners. Chairs are light narrow wooden pieces with delicate joints and a short stepped highlight on the backrest, visually different from the chunky permanent table legs. Pots have a thin bright rim and a distinctive simple clay shape, clearly separate from the floor and wall.
Do not add glowing outlines, star icons, floating labels or health bars. The breakable family should be readable through shape, assembly and consistent small highlights, not through a gameplay UI.
Demonstrate three visual states naturally and sparingly in the environment: several INTACT breakable props with the same family traits, ONE crate with a clear loose split plank / damaged corner in a storage edge group, and ONE small SHATTERED POT with a few flat terracotta shards beside the shop's lower outer wall, away from doorways. Shards are low, sparse and leave the ground visibly open; no cloud or big rubble pile. Keep the rest of the map mostly clean. Do not make all objects look broken.
Do not scatter extra cover randomly in the central square. Place light crates at loading/storage edges and chairs near card tables. Keep reasonable movement gaps among furniture.

IDENTITIES AND SCALE:
Exactly four small grounded characters at the same relative scale as reference 1, around 35-42 image pixels high on a 1600x1000 image. Poncho in the saloon: broad straw-gold sombrero with raised olive crown, long brown vertically hanging cloth covering feet, fringed hem touching the floor, small attached contact shadow. Garcia in the square: charcoal hat with small gold star, violet shoulders and red scarf. Brown cowboy hat / blue scarf placeholder on the upper side street. Pale hat / charcoal crown / ochre outfit placeholder inside the shop. Preserve their silhouettes and colors. No NPCs, duplicates or extra portraits.
Exactly ONE small GREEN TEQUILA BOTTLE on the central square. No green decorative bottles elsewhere; saloon shelves hold ceramic mugs/jugs.

SINGLE FINAL CLEAN MAP:
Keep the saloon on the left, goods shop right, fenced yard top-right, tool shed bottom-left and closed homes at the perimeter. Orthographic overhead 2D room projection, roofs removed only from accessible buildings, not isometric or perspective. One single coherent game-map illustration, no panels, inset or comparison strip.
No text, signage lettering, titles, labels, numbers, HUD, alpha overlay, route lines, icons, circles, arrows, coloured path paint, combat effects, gunfire, speed trails, gore, watermark or frame. This is an art-direction concept, not a claim of measured collision or gameplay validation.
Before finalizing, ensure every listed opening is a CLEAR EMPTY GAP in the wall silhouette, not a closed door, and there are still exactly four characters.
intent: New artistic iteration after reference study; visible openings and breakable families, no game implementation
